title: Homepage Hero
emotion: Arrival. Anticipation. The road ahead at the best hour of the day.
direction: Coastal or mountain road identity. Blue hour, dusk or night. The vehicle's own lighting signature is the brightest thing in frame. Wide and cinematic, with space on the left for copy.
searches: sports car night reflections wet road

title: SUVs
emotion: Adventure. Dust, mountains, capability — a family that goes places.
direction: Vehicle in landscape, not in a car park. Gravel, mountain pass, open country. Warm low light.

title: Sedans
emotion: Composure. The classic shape, executed properly.
direction: Clean profile or three-quarter. Restrained setting. Evening or overcast light. Modern car — not a period piece.

title: Hatchbacks
emotion: City life. Compact confidence, easy to live with.
direction: Urban setting, clean architecture, daylight or city lights. Modern car, well kept, photographed with intent.

title: Bakkies
emotion: South African utility and adventure. Work hard, then escape.
direction: Pickup in genuine terrain — bush, farm, mountain track, river crossing. Dust or mud welcome. Never a forecourt.

title: Luxury
emotion: Night. City. Glass and lighting. Quiet money.
direction: Dark, reflective surfaces. Architectural backdrop. No daylight. Restraint over flash — a car that does not need to announce itself.

title: Electric
emotion: Minimal. Clean. Modern. The quiet future.
direction: Uncluttered composition, cool light, modern architecture. Charging imagery is welcome where it is elegant rather than instructional.

title: Performance
emotion: Track. Motion. Aggression held in check.
direction: Panning or motion blur, circuit or mountain road. Low angle. Never static in a car park.

title: People carriers
emotion: Everyone, and everything they bring. Calm competence.
direction: Van or MPV in a real setting. Space and practicality implied, never stated. Family present or implied, not posed.

title: Convertibles
direction: Roof down, coastal road, warm low sun. The feeling of a Sunday with nowhere to be.

title: Dealer Showrooms
note: Interiors. Used on dealer public profiles, where the job is to make a dealership feel like a building the buyer has walked into. The cars in frame are incidental — the architecture and the light are the subject.
emotion: You have arrived somewhere serious. Quiet, lit, and expensive to run.
direction: Interior architecture. Polished floor, controlled lighting, glass and clean structural lines. Wide enough to read as a space rather than a display stand. No crowds, no signage, no paperwork on desks.

title: Dealership Exteriors
note: Cover photography for dealer profiles. Architecture, not signage — a building that looks like it is worth walking into. Variety across candidates matters here more than anywhere: these are covers for many different dealerships and one building reused everywhere is worse than none.
emotion: Arrival at a serious showroom. Architecture, not signage.
direction: Modern dealership or gallery architecture from outside. Glass, light, clean lines, ideally at dusk when the interior lighting reads. Wide letterbox crop.

title: Lifestyle
note: People, and the part of their life a car is in. Used behind editorial sections and wherever the product needs to be about a person rather than a vehicle. Nobody should look like a stock model: no thumbs up, no handshake over a desk, no keys held to camera.
emotion: The good part. The drive there, the arrival, the door closing.
direction: Natural light, unposed, one or two people. Loading a boot, a hand on a wheel, a family arriving somewhere. Warm and specific rather than aspirational and generic.
searches: dog in car window road trip

title: Cape Town
note: Surf4Cars is a South African marketplace and should look like one. This is the identity set: place before product. Used for hero alternates, editorial plates and regional pages.
emotion: Home. The mountain, the coast, and a road worth taking the long way round.
direction: Cape Town and the Western Cape. Table Mountain, Chapman's Peak, Camps Bay, the coastal roads, city at blue hour. A car in frame is a bonus, not a requirement. Wide, cinematic, and unmistakably this place.

title: Editorial — Why Buyers Choose Surf4Cars
note: The full-bleed plate behind the homepage's editorial section. Judged almost entirely on its quiet area: the copy sits over the left third, so a candidate with a beautiful subject dead centre is the wrong candidate.
emotion: Confidence, held still. The decision has already been made and it was the right one.
direction: One vehicle small in a large landscape, or an open road at the end of the day. Low sun or blue hour. The right two-thirds may be busy; the left third must be near-empty and low-contrast so white type holds without a scrim.

title: Promotional Banners
note: A banner is a photographic plate plus SURF typography. This brief selects the plate only — the type is composed in-house over the approved image, so a candidate must hold a large quiet area for copy.
emotion: Editorial confidence. The image carries the message before a word is read.
direction: Wide letterbox crop. One dominant subject, large negative space on one side. Low contrast in the copy zone so white type holds without a scrim.

title: Dealer Logos
note: A real dealer's logo is that dealer's trademark and is uploaded by them — it can never be sourced from a stock library. What the platform actually needs curating is the FALLBACK mark shown when a dealership has not uploaded one. Candidates are generated from the SURF brand system, so no third-party licence applies.
emotion: A dealership that has not uploaded a logo should still look like it belongs here.
direction: Monogram from the dealership initials. Restrained, single accent, works at 40px and 160px, legible on both light and dark cards.
